handbookNote: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual (base AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' content, cover Version: September 9, 2022, with most section footers dated Version: July 2017 -- Sections 11 and 12 in the base manual itself already carry the Version: September 9, 2022 modernized text), published by the New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV), a division of the NH Department of Safety -- fetched directly from https://www.dmv.nh.gov/sites/g/files/ehbemt416/files/inline-documents/nhcdm.pdf on 2026-08-23 (4.7MB PDF; the DMV's Akamai edge network returned 'Access Denied' to direct curl/WebFetch requests, so the file was retrieved via an authenticated in-browser fetch() call from the DMV's own site and saved via a blob download, then verified as a valid PDF before extraction). Full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/nh_cdl_research/nhcdm_full.txt (9,333 lines), cross-checked against a pdftotext -raw extraction (nhcdm_raw.txt, 12,378 lines) for two-column sections. A companion 'Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement for Modernized Version' (Version: September 9, 2022, with Section 12M carrying an additional 'Update 2/9/2024' revision), fetched the same way from https://www.dmv.nh.gov/sites/g/files/ehbemt416/files/inline-documents/nhcdm-s.pdf on 2026-08-23 (1.1MB PDF, extracted to nhcdm-s_full.txt, 1,082 lines), republishes Section 11 as Section 11M (Vehicle Inspection Test) and Section 12 as Section 12M (Basic Control Skills Test) with the most current item-by-item inspection/scoring language; the supplement was used as the primary source for this track's vehicle-inspection and basic-control-skills buckets, cross-checked against the base manual's own (nearly identical) Section 11/12 text. Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics: New Hampshire's own official sources -- the base manual, the supplement, and the NH DMV's 'Commercial Driver Licenses' and 'CDL Road Test' webpages (both fetched directly and read in full via browser on 2026-08-23) -- do NOT disclose a specific per-test item count or numeric passing-score percentage anywhere; this is a genuine gap in the official source, not an oversight, consistent with several other states built in this project (e.g. Alabama, Arkansas, Kansas, Indiana, Maine, Nebraska, Mississippi, Minnesota, Maryland). The federally standardized minimum passing score of 80 percent applies regardless (49 CFR 383.135(a)). Third-party CDL test-prep sites (e.g. dmv-permit-test.com, driving-tests.org, cristcdl.com, cdlpracticetest.com) converge on a General Knowledge test of 50 questions requiring 40 correct (80%) to pass, consistent with the common AAMVA-battery default, but this is NOT confirmed by New Hampshire's own official manual or DMV site and is cited here only as third-party corroboration, not as a verified official figure -- treat all item counts as unconfirmed/hedged in this track's exam-mechanics copy. New Hampshire's three CDL vehicle classes are A (combination, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR), B (single vehicle or combination with towed unit 10,000 lbs GVWR or less, GVWR 26,001+ lbs), and C (vehicle not meeting A/B, but designed to carry 16+ passengers including the driver, or requiring hazmat placarding, or carrying a 42 CFR Part 73 select agent/toxin). New Hampshire's six CDL endorsements are H (Hazardous Materials), N (Tank Vehicle), P (Passenger), S (School Bus), T (Double/Triple Trailers), and X (combined Tank Vehicle and Hazardous Materials); only P, S, and N may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP). New Hampshire requires federally mandated Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT), verified via the FMCSA Training Provider Registry, before a first-time Class A/B CDL, a classification upgrade, or a first-time P/S/H endorsement, and this training must be completed before an applicant can schedule a skills test. A Hazmat endorsement (new, renewal, or transfer from another state) requires TSA fingerprint-based security threat assessment clearance obtained before visiting the DMV. Written tests are generally waived when transferring a valid out-of-state CDL with matching class/endorsements, except Hazmat, which always requires the knowledge test. New Hampshire offers a CDL skills-test waiver for eligible active-duty military members and veterans (within 12 months of honorable/general discharge) who are NH residents trained in heavy-vehicle operation and hold a Commanding Officer's certification -- the written knowledge test(s) must still be passed. CDL renewal requires passing a vision test plus endorsement-specific requirements (e.g., a current Hazmat TSA clearance and knowledge-test pass, or current school-bus-roster proof and a certificate knowledge-test pass). Content-depth rationale: New Hampshire uses the same AAMVA-authored 'Modernized Testing System' base manual as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Missouri, Nebraska), organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction (CDL classes, endorsements/restrictions, disqualifications, other safety rules), Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section at 43 manual pages, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering vehicle inspection, basic control, shifting, seeing/mirrors, communicating, speed/space management, hazard perception, distracted/aggressive driving, and night driving/fatigue; 03_driving_safely_b covering fog, winter and hot-weather driving, railroad crossings, mountain driving, driving emergencies, antilock braking systems, skid control/recovery, accident procedures, fires, and alcohol/drugs/staying alert), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (22 manual pages, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering the intent of the regulations, shipper/carrier responsibilities, communication rules, and placarding; 11_hazmat_b covering loading/unloading, driving/parking rules, emergencies, and the glossary), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11M/11 Vehicle Inspection (modernized, per the supplement), Section 12M/12 Basic Control Skills Test (modernized, per the supplement), and Section 13 On-Road Driving (13 and 12M combined into one bucket, 14_basic_control_onroad). Some sections (Transporting Cargo Safely at 3 pages, Tank Vehicles at 2 pages, Doubles and Triples and Transporting Passengers Safely at 4 pages each) are naturally very short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. No New Hampshire-specific administrative front matter (fees, CLP hold-time tables, residency rules, etc.) is inserted into either PDF beyond what is described above from the DMV's own webpages; every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official New Hampshire manual/supplement text or, where noted, the DMV's own CDL webpages, cited in that question's source_note -- none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
